Title: Document 3
Content: Source: Livy, Roman historian, History of Rome, `text(first century B.C.E.)`, describing the capture of the Greek region of Epirus by the Romans in `text(167 B.C.E.)`

Early in the morning all the gold and silver had been brought together, and in the `text(fourth hour)` the signal was given for the soldiers to sack the cities. So great was the plunder that `400` denarii* were appointed to `text(each cavalryman)` and `200` to `text(each foot soldier)`, and `150text(,)000` human beings were led away into slavery. Then the walls of the plundered cities were razed; these cities numbered about `text(seventy)`. The plunder was sold, and the soldiers' shares paid out of the proceeds.
